1: The noble Avalokiteshvara, the Bodhisattva of great compassion, while practising deeply the perfection of wisdom, looked down from on high and saw the five aggregates — form, feeling, perception, impulse, and consciousness — and saw that in their own being they are empty.

Here, O Shariputra, form is emptiness, and emptiness is form. Emptiness is not other than form; form is not other than emptiness. Whatever is form, that is emptiness; whatever is emptiness, that is form. The same is true of feelings, perceptions, impulses, and consciousness.

Here, O Shariputra, all things are marked by emptiness: they are not born, nor do they cease; they are not stained, nor are they purified; they do not increase, and they do not diminish. Therefore in emptiness there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no impulse, no consciousness.

There is no eye, no ear, no nose, no tongue, no body, no mind; no sight, no sound, no smell, no taste, no touch, no thing of mind; no realm of sight, even to no realm of mind-consciousness. There is no ignorance, and no ending of ignorance; there is no old age and death, and no ending of old age and death.

There is no suffering, no origin of suffering, no cessation of suffering, no path; no wisdom, no attainment, and no non-attainment. Therefore, O Shariputra, since there is no attainment, the bodhisattva lives depending on the perfection of wisdom, and the mind is without obstacle. Without obstacle, there is no fear; passing utterly beyond false views, one attains final nirvana.

Therefore know the perfection of wisdom as the great mantra, the mantra of great knowledge, the utmost mantra, the unequalled mantra, the allayer of every suffering, true because not in vain. And of the perfection of wisdom this is the mantra that is spoken: Gone, gone, gone beyond, gone utterly beyond — O awakening, hail!
